stops.note: combined 'teotl' (god) and 'cintli' (dried maize), naming the wild ancestor grass of corn
stops.meaning: god's maize, a wild grass related to corn
a wild grass, the ancestor of cultivated corn

stops.note: George Beadle's 1930s research showed teosinte is maize's wild ancestor
stops.meaning: a wild grass related to maize

stops.note: borrowed into English botanical and genetic terminology
stops.meaning: a wild grass considered the evolutionary ancestor of modern corn

current_meaning: a wild grass native to Mexico and Central America, recognized as the evolutionary ancestor of modern corn
